newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee slumps on speculative dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee slumps on speculative dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was driven down by speculative demand for the dollar and slight import covering, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.33 to the dollar, after opening at 57.12. The rupee closed at 57.09 on Tuesday.
"Speculators were banking on the Central Bank pushing up the dollar in line with overseas movements," said a Seylan Bank dealer.
The Central Bank has pushed up the dollar by 22 cents in the last 10 working days, in line with international movements dealers said.
Overnight call money closed at 12.5 percent, with the market well offered, they said.
Friday money, however was dealt at 14 percent, which some dealers said was unusual, given the market's high level of liquidity.
